headline: Level on points, level in the market at Fratton Park
summary: Portsmouth and Millwall meet at Fratton Park level on points: both on 15 points, both with a goal difference of zero. The market sees the same picture — Portsmouth are 36.1% favourites to Millwall's 35.7%, and the handicap is level, so neither side is rated a goal better. What separates them is who can play. Portsmouth are missing at least 10 players and had only 4 days since Wolves; Millwall have had a full week but are on their fifth goalkeeper of the season and may be without both main strikers. The fair goals total is 2.43.
read: Portsmouth and Millwall arrive on identical records — 15 points, 12th and 13th — and the market cannot split them, pricing Portsmouth at 36.1% and Millwall at 35.7% with a level handicap. The difference is who is available: Portsmouth are down at least ten players while Millwall are on their fifth goalkeeper of the season and may be missing both main forwards, and Millwall are the fresher side with seven days' rest against Portsmouth's four.

facts.fact: Portsmouth are missing at least 10 players through injury, and boss John Mousinho said they are hoping to have bodies back for the Millwall game.
facts.meaning: Portsmouth go into a Saturday lunchtime home game with a threadbare squad, so rotation and who is actually available matters more than usual.

facts.fact: Millwall goalkeeper Filip Marschall is out for an extended spell with ankle ligament damage suffered against Lincoln, and Millwall are set to make their fifth goalkeeper change of the season.
facts.meaning: A settled defence in front of a keeper who has barely played is the biggest single question hanging over Millwall's trip to Fratton Park.

facts.fact: Millwall striker T. Arconte, who has 3 goals in 638 minutes this season, is listed as doubtful with an ankle injury, and J. Coburn (2 goals) is out with a muscle injury.
facts.meaning: Millwall may be without both of the forwards who have carried their scoring, which puts the load on a side already averaging 1.68 xG for per game.

facts.fact: Portsmouth are narrow favourites at 36.1% to Millwall's 35.7%, with the draw at 28.2%.
facts.meaning: The market sees this as close to a coin-flip: home advantage is the only thing separating the two sides.

facts.fact: The handicap sits at level (+0), with the market's fair line at zero goals and the two sides split 50.1% to 49.9%.
facts.meaning: The market does not rate either team a goal better — a one-goal win either way is priced as the swing factor, and the draw is fully in play.

facts.fact: Portsmouth have lost one of their last seven Championship matches, drawing 1-1 at Wolves on Tuesday through a late Terry Devlin equaliser.
facts.meaning: Portsmouth arrive unbeaten in six of seven but on a short turnaround, having had to chase the game at Molineux.

facts.fact: Millwall created 1.87 xG against Lincoln City and came back from two goals down to draw 2-2.
facts.meaning: Millwall are making chances even when results go against them — their 1.68 xG-for average across the last five is the higher of the two teams.

facts.fact: Portsmouth played at Wolves on Tuesday, four days before kick-off; Millwall have had seven days since their 2-2 with Lincoln.
facts.meaning: Millwall are the fresher side for a lunchtime kick-off, and Portsmouth's short week comes with Mousinho having already rested four players at Wolves with this game in mind.

sources.fact: Portsmouth are missing at least 10 players through injury and boss John Mousinho said they are hoping to have bodies back for Millwall.
Portsmouth drew 1-1 at Wolves with a late Terry Devlin equaliser and have lost just one of their last seven Championship matches.
Mousinho rested Marlon Pack, Zak Swanson, Ryan Kavuma-McQueen and Marko Milovanovic at Wolves, targeting the Millwall game as the more realistic proposition.
Thomas Waddingham could return for Portsmouth against Millwall after being unavailable for the Wolves fixture.
Mousinho gave a pre-Millwall interview on Wednesday, October 21st.
Millwall goalkeeper Filip Marschall faces an extended spell out with ankle ligament damage suffered against Lincoln City.
Millwall are set to make their fifth goalkeeper change of the season for the Portsmouth trip.
Alex Neil confirmed an extended absence for a summer signing in another injury blow for Millwall.
